mainProgression.progression: i - VII6 - VI6 - V7 - iv7 - i6 - iiø7 - V7
mainProgression.description: Classical stepwise bass descent from F# down through E, D, and C#, followed by a cycle through Bm7, F#m/A, and half-diminished iiø7.

sectionProgressions.description: Four-bar classical nylon descending progression with suspended upper chord melody
Rich circle-of-fifths voice leading with half-diminished ii chord leading to major dominant V7
Expands into fuller fingerpicked textures supporting Sting's contemplative vocal

harmonicFunction: F#m (i) - Somber minor tonic established with low 2nd-fret bass note
E6 (VII6) - First stepwise bass drop (F# → E) providing smooth classical continuity
D6 (VI6) - Second stepwise bass drop (E → D) maintaining harmonic descent
C#7 (V7) - Classical major dominant containing the E# leading tone pulling decisively back into F#m
G#m7b5 (iiø7) - Half-diminished chord providing sophisticated jazz/classical transition to V7

techniques.name: Classical Nylon-String PIMA Arpeggiation
techniques.description: Using classical thumb-index-middle-ring (PIMA) fingerpicking to cleanly articulate bass notes on the beat while weaving intricate arpeggio patterns on strings 2, 3, and 4

notes: Bass notes: F# (2nd fret low E), E (open low E), D (5th fret A string), C# (4th fret A string)
Inner voices: Ringing dyads on strings 4, 3, and 2
Delicate finger pressure to prevent fret buzz on nylon or acoustic strings
sequence: Pluck the low F# bass note with the thumb (P)
Follow with index (I) on string 4, middle (M) on string 3, and ring (A) on string 2
Shift bass notes smoothly on beats 1 and 3 without interrupting upper voice sustain
Nail the stretch on the G#m7b5 chord shape
tips: Play near the soundhole (tasto) for a round, warm classical tone
Keep your right-hand thumb positioned forward of your fingers to prevent collisions
Dominic Miller composed this on a nylon-string classical guitar—nylon string tension makes the wide stretches easier

techniques.name: Descending Bass Voice Leading & Half-Diminished Harmony
techniques.description: Navigating the sophisticated harmonic turnaround from Bm7 to F#m/A, G#m7b5, and C#7, maintaining melodic independence between the moving bassline and upper-string classical intervals

notes: G#m7b5 shape: 4-X-4-4-3-X (requiring a wide 4-fret reach with pinky on fret 4 and index on fret 3)
Stepwise bass motion: B (fret 2 A) to A (open A) to G# (fret 4 low E) to C# (fret 4 A)
Voice leading: Sustained common tones on strings 2 and 3 connect the changing root notes
sequence: Isolate the G#m7b5 chord fingering slowly at 60 BPM until all four fretted strings ring clearly
Practice the resolution from the half-diminished iiø7 into the C#7 dominant chord
Maintain seamless PIMA right-hand plucking without stopping the sixteenth-note momentum
Fade the final repetition with gentle finger pad strokes near the 12th fret
tips: Arch your left-hand knuckles high to prevent muting the adjacent G string note on G#m7b5
Keep the right-hand thumb relaxed when shifting between strings 6, 5, and 4
Let each bass note sustain for its full half-note value to preserve the classical counterpoint

sections.name: Main Classical Nylon-String Arpeggio
sections.description: Dominic Miller's legendary nylon-string opening figure, one of the most sampled acoustic riffs in modern music.
notes: Let the bass notes ring as pedal tones
Execute the delicate upper-voice voice leading
Keep an unhurried, expressive 84 BPM tempo

sections.name: Turnaround Voice Leading (Bm7 to G#m7b5)
sections.description: The second half of the main theme introducing Bm7 and the haunting G#m7b5 half-diminished chord.
notes: Fret G#m7b5 with index on 4th fret low E and ring on 4th fret D
Smooth resolution to the C#7 shape
Maintain pure nylon string tone

sections.name: Verse 1 Intimate Acoustic Accompaniment
sections.description: Sting enters with his narrative vocal as the nylon-string guitar settles into an intimate, warm accompaniment.
notes: Soft dynamic touch under the vocal phrases
Sustain the 2nd-fret bass notes cleanly
Maintain steady PIMA finger arpeggio rhythm

sections.name: Chorus Hook ('He deals the cards as a meditation')
sections.description: The broader chordal framework underpinning the chorus hook 'I know that the spades are the swords of a soldier'.
notes: Wider dynamic volume during the vocal hook
Full chord arpeggios spanning 5 strings
Gentle natural deceleration before returning to the verse

sections.name: Harmonica Interlude & Subtle Nylon Embellishments
sections.description: Larry Adler's chromatic harmonica solo takes center stage while Miller weaves subtle grace-note variations through the F#m progression.
sections.progression: i - VII6 - VI6 - V7 - iv7 - iiø7 - V7
notes: Leave space for the harmonica melody to soar
Subtle tone variations between tasto and ponticello
Even right-hand dynamics across all 8 bars

sections.name: Final Chorus & Gentle F#m Nylon Outro Cadence
sections.description: The transcendent final chorus resolving into a slow, delicate restatement of the main motif, ending on an unresolved, resonant chord.
notes: Gradual ritardando over the final four bars
Delicate pad-of-finger attack on the closing chord
Allow the final F# minor triad to ring into complete silence

beginner.title: Chord Shapes & Bass Descent
steps: Learn the four fundamental chord shapes: F#m, E, D, and C#7
Practice the descending bassline on the lower strings (F# → E → D → C#)
Play simple thumb-and-finger strums at 60 BPM

intermediate.title: PIMA Fingerpicking Pattern
steps: Internalize the exact thumb-index-middle-ring fingerpicking cycle
Coordinate the shifting bass notes with continuous upper-string arpeggios
Smoothly execute the transition into the G#m7b5 chord

advanced.title: Concert Fluency & Tone Nuance
steps: Play the entire 4-minute composition with fluid classical touch and zero buzzing
Control dynamic swell between quiet verses and expressive chorus peaks
Perform cleanly on nylon strings without relying on heavy compression

commonMistakes: Rushing the tempo (keep it strictly at 84 BPM)
Collapsing your right-hand wrist causing the fingernails to click against strings
Muting the high notes during the wide fret stretch on the G#m7b5 chord
practiceRoutine: 5 minutes: Right-hand PIMA arpeggio drill on open strings
10 minutes: First 4-bar progression shifting with metronome at 70-84 BPM
15 minutes: Turnaround chord stretch (Bm7 → F#m/A → G#m7b5 → C#7)
focusAreas: PIMA fingerpicking independence and tone consistency
Wide-stretch clarity on the half-diminished G#m7b5 voicing
Smooth classical voice-leading between shifting bass roots
metronomeWork: Practice at 65, 75, and 84 BPM, focusing on even sixteenth-note subdivisions
